scope: Source-bound maintainer science-explanation review, supplemented by actual browser disclosure/search checks. No student comprehension trial or validation of scientific prediction accuracy.
reviewed_distinctions: Isomers share formula; constitutional versus spatial differences, conformers involve nuclear motions; resonance drawings are electronic bookkeeping for one nuclear arrangement.
R/S follows CIP configuration, not rotation of the view or a general mapping to measured (+)/(−) optical rotation.
Calculated harmonic modes do not establish experimental peak assignments; equilibrium and ground-state rotational constants are distinguished.
Optimization convergence, search or imported structures do not prove a minimum, global completeness or physical equilibrium populations.

isomers.title: Isomers, conformers and resonance drawings
isomers.what: Isomers have the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms. Constitutional isomers have different connections; stereoisomers differ in spatial arrangement. Enantiomers are mirror-image stereoisomers; diastereomers are stereoisomers that are not mirror images, such as E/Z alkene pairs.
isomers.why: These differences can affect energy, reactivity and spectra. You need to know which structures you are comparing before interpreting an energy difference.
isomers.when: Use this when importing several structures, doing a conformer search or comparing calculated isomers.
isomers.where: Upload separate candidate structures through Your files. Calculations → Advanced: other calculation tools → Other structures and energies contains conformer-search tools; Results compares compatible calculated structures.
how: First compare which atoms are connected. If connections differ, you have different constitutional structures.
For the same connections, consider spatial arrangement. Conformers differ through motions such as bond rotation or ring puckering; their ease of interconversion depends on the barrier and conditions.
Resonance drawings show alternative electron bookkeeping for the same nuclear arrangement. Do not treat them as separate molecules or conformers to rank.
Only compare energies from scientifically compatible calculations, and keep unknown energies unknown.
limitations: A few candidate geometries do not establish every possible isomer or the global minimum.
A duplicate-removal test does not prove that retained candidates are stable minima or equilibrium populations.

chirality.title: Chirality and R/S labels
chirality.what: A chiral structure cannot be superimposed on its mirror image by rotating and moving it. Such a mirror-image pair is called a pair of enantiomers.
chirality.why: A drawing's appearance depends on your viewing direction. Confusing a rotated view with a different configuration can lead to a wrong molecular assignment.
chirality.when: Check stereochemistry when your assignment concerns chiral molecules or when importing or building stereochemical structures.
chirality.where: Inspect the selected structure in Calculations → Starting structure. Use your chemical drawing and instructor's stereochemical assignment alongside the 3D view.
how: Verify the connections and substituents, then check the specified stereochemistry in the source structure.
R/S labels follow the Cahn–Ingold–Prelog priority rules for the relevant stereogenic feature; they are not labels for the direction you rotate the image.
The signs (+)/(−) describe measured optical rotation under stated conditions. R does not generally mean (+), and S does not generally mean (−).
limitations: The viewer is not an automatic stereochemical assignment or optical-rotation measurement tool.
Enantiomers have the same ordinary rotational constants and many other properties in an achiral environment; those values alone cannot distinguish them.

spectroscopy.title: Calculated properties and experimental spectra
spectroscopy.what: Spectroscopy studies how matter interacts with radiation. Different experiments, such as rotational, infrared and NMR spectroscopy, probe different properties.
spectroscopy.why: A calculated frequency or rotational constant is a model prediction. It is not automatically an observed experimental peak or a complete measured spectrum.
spectroscopy.when: Use this before interpreting the supported calculated observables or comparing them with an assigned experiment.
spectroscopy.where: Under More scientific tools, Spectra and properties reads supported native outputs and provides rotational-property, Hessian/isotope and numerical-data inspection tools.
how: Identify what the displayed quantity actually is: a rotational constant, harmonic vibrational mode or supplied numerical observation.
Check units and whether a constant describes equilibrium geometry (Ae, Be, Ce) or includes nuclear-motion effects (A0, B0, C0).
Compare a model prediction with the same type of experimental observable, using the method's stated limitations.
Keep assignments, raw outputs and any experimental source separate in your report.
limitations: A harmonic mode is not proof of an experimental IR peak assignment; intensities, selection rules, conditions and anharmonic effects matter.
This help does not enable NMR prediction, an experimental IR analysis pipeline or automatic spectral identification.

conformer_search.title: Search for alternative conformations
conformer_search.what: A conformer search explores alternative nuclear arrangements of the intended molecule or complex and retains candidate structures.
conformer_search.why: One optimized starting geometry can miss other arrangements. A search helps identify candidates for later qualified calculations.
conformer_search.when: Use it when your assignment explicitly requires conformational exploration and the needed search engine is available.
conformer_search.where: Calculations → Advanced: other calculation tools → Other structures and energies. Use its available Calculation / Method choices and Start TOPOS calculation.
how: Check the intended structure and electronic state, then select the assigned supported search protocol and bounds.
Read the search status and any partial or unavailable outcome.
Inspect retained structures and use qualified follow-up calculations before ranking physical minima or populations.
limitations: Searches do not prove completeness or that every candidate is a minimum.
Do not loosen duplicate thresholds to discard inconvenient candidates. Unknown or incompatible energies must not be ranked as measured values.

calculation_types.title: What task should the program perform?
calculation_types.what: A single point evaluates energy at the supplied geometry. Optimization changes allowed nuclear coordinates. Frequencies examine local energy curvature.
calculation_types.why: These tasks answer different questions. An energy at one geometry does not improve that geometry or establish a minimum.
calculation_types.when: Choose the operation named in your assignment before pressing the run button.
calculation_types.where: 3 · Run assigned calculation / Calculations → Run calculation. The operation controls depend on the selected calculation computer and engine.
how: For energy at a specified geometry, use the assigned single-point operation.
For a nearby stationary structure, use the assigned optimization operation and inspect convergence.
When the protocol calls for minimum classification, inspect appropriate frequencies at the optimized geometry as well.
Read the current run-button label: it changes with the selected engine and task.
limitations: Optimization does not prove a global minimum, or even a local minimum without suitable classification.
Only operations with a verified available provider can run; selecting a task cannot supply a missing scientific capability.

convergence_frequencies.title: Did optimization find a meaningful structure?
convergence_frequencies.what: Convergence means specified numerical stopping criteria were met. It is different from demonstrating chemical accuracy or finding a minimum.
convergence_frequencies.why: A normal exit or nearly unchanged energy can coexist with unconverged forces, an incorrect electronic state or a saddle point.
convergence_frequencies.when: Read these checks before using a calculated geometry, energy or spectrum in a report.
convergence_frequencies.where: Retrieve the calculation in Calculations, then inspect its result and warnings under 4 · Read and save results / Results. Frequency and Hessian tools are in Spectra and properties.
how: Check electronic SCF convergence separately from geometry energy, gradient and displacement convergence.
For a claimed unconstrained minimum, examine vibrational curvature after overall translation and rotation are removed.
An imaginary mode indicates negative curvature; inspect its motion and numerical conditions. A small imaginary value can also reflect numerical problems or a shallow surface.
Keep constrained results labelled: they minimize only the coordinates allowed to move.
limitations: Optimization completion is not proof of the lowest-energy isomer or experimental accuracy.
Do not delete modes, relax thresholds or ignore a warning simply to label a structure a minimum.
